title: Method for design of information security system for sensitive data leak prevention
venue: Journal of Data Science and Intelligent Systems (JDSIS)
abstract: This article proposes a top-down method for designing an information security system (ISS) that prevents the leakage of sensitive information outside the organization. The method combines systems analysis with the IEEE 1471 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 architecture description standards to construct stakeholder-specific conceptual models and a multi-layered conceptual ISS architecture. Two formal transformations are defined: T₁ converts the conceptual model into an object-oriented model represented via the Unified Modeling Language (UML), while T₂ converts this model into an agent-based simulation model. The method is compared against NIST Special Publication 800-37, the ISO/IEC 27005:2022 standard, the SABSA (Sherwood Applied Business Security Architecture) framework, and the TOGAF framework (Table 1). A one-year field study across seven organizations (five public and two private)—in which the ISS was implemented on a Data Leak Prevention (DLP) platform—demonstrated an average 42.1% reduction in policy violation incidents (Wilcoxon criterion W = 0, p = 0.016, effect size dz = 3.50 for paired samples), as well as an increase in the composite ISO/IEC 27004-based compliance score from 18.7% to 86.4%. An agent-based prototype (implemented in the NetLogo environment, using 50 Monte Carlo simulations) reproduces a reduction in the same direction and of comparable magnitude in a simulation environment (in silico). title: Design of Information Security Systems for internal threat protection
venue: Springer series “Communications in Computer and Information Science”
publisher: Springer series “Communications in Computer and Information Science”
abstract: The article discusses a method for designing and creating an information security system (ISS) in organizations. The method considers different viewpoints on the system, presenting different requirements for it from dif-ferent specialties involved in the design of the system. The problem with the participation of different specialists comes from the fact that they are expressed through different means of expression (contracts, laws, descrip-tions, engineering drawings, program code, etc.). In addition, different terms are used, which may have different meanings in different specialties. There-fore, when designing an ISS, it is vital to use a method that translates all re-quirements into a single universal language understandable to all special-ties. Such a method for designing an ISS in organizations is presented be-low. We have called the method "Reversed Tower of Babylon", which does the opposite of the legend of the Tower of Babel - unifies the language so that it is understandable to all specialists involved in the design of the ISS. The method provides platform independence, through which systems are created that are independent of specific platforms and environments and fulfil the conditions set for them. The article discusses the design and im-plementation of ISS to protect against internal threats in a given organiza-tion with a focus on the human factor as a threat, or the so-called insiders. The system is based on a Data Leak Prevention (DLP) environment.
